My name is what it is, and I am a man with a small piece of land here in Zomba. This sorghum plot, I plant it because sorghum does not fear when the rains come late — it still gives me something for the family. I do not waste the fertilizer coupons on sorghum; if I get any from FISP, I put it on my maize plot where it helps more. On this sorghum plot I will throw some manure from my goats and chickens, and I intercrop with pigeon pea so the soil stays alive. I use the seed I kept from last year's harvest — the local one my father grew — because hybrid sorghum seed is not something we find in our area, and I have no money to buy it.
